![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14060128/assets/73c6a8268a179f72611fb65e099d1249d48501e4fd4731d03747800e1944fd97.png)

The path ${C}_{1}$ consists of a the line segment from the point $A(0,1)$ to the point $B(1,2),$ and the path ${C}_{2}$ consists of a line segment from the point $B(1,2)$ to the point $D(1,3).$

Given that ${\int }_{{C}_{2}}F\cdot \text{d}r=\frac{7}{2},$ evaluate ${\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r,$ where $F(x,y)=(2x-3y)\,i+(x+y)\,j,$ and $C={C}_{1}\cup {C}_{2}.$
worked_solution:
We will use the fact that

$$
{\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r={\int }_{{C}_{1}}F\cdot \text{d}r+{\int }_{{C}_{2}}F\cdot \text{d}r.
$$

We're given the value of the second integral, so we only need to work out the first.

The path ${C}_{1}$ is the line segment from $A$ to $B.$  It can be parametrized as

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{1}(t) & =a+t(b-a) \\  & =⟨0,1⟩+t(⟨1,2⟩-⟨0,1⟩) \\  & =⟨t,1+t⟩ \\  & =t\,i+(1+t)\,j,\end{aligned}
$$

where $0<t<1.$ Along this segment, we have $x=t$ and $y=1+t.$ Therefore, 

$$
\begin{aligned}F({r}_{1}(t)) & =(2x-3y)\,i+(x+y)\,j \\  & =(2t-3(1+t))\,i+(t+(1+t))\,j \\  & =(-3-t)\,i+(2t+1)\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

Computing the derivative, we get the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{1}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t)i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(1+t)j \\  & =i+j\end{aligned}
$$

We can now compute the dot product:

$$
\begin{aligned}F({r}_{1}(t))\cdot {r}_{1}^{′}(t) & =((-3-t)\,i+(2t+1)\,j)\cdot (i+j) \\  & =-3-t+2t+1 \\  & =t-2\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we can evaluate the integral, as follows: 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r & ={\int }_{{C}_{1}}F\cdot \text{d}r+{\int }_{{C}_{2}}F\cdot \text{d}r \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}F({r}_{1}(t))\cdot {r}_{1}^{′}(t)\,\text{d}t+\frac{7}{2} \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}(t-2)\,\text{d}t+\frac{7}{2} \\  & ={[\frac{{t}^{2}}{2}-2t]}_{0}^{1}+\frac{7}{2} \\  & =[\frac{1}{2}-2-0]+\frac{7}{2} \\  & =-\frac{3}{2}+\frac{7}{2} \\  & =2\end{aligned}
$$
